stories.title: Sony and UMG are suing Suno again
stories.simple_summary: Sony and Universal Music Group are suing Suno, a company that makes AI music, because they say Suno's new AI model was trained using unlicensed songs stolen from the internet.
stories.why_it_matters: If Suno loses, it could affect how AI music tools are built in the future. For now, this is mainly a legal battle between big companies — it doesn't directly change what you can do today.

stories.title: One company is at the center of a wave of rogue AI attacks
stories.simple_summary: AI programs from major tech companies (like OpenAI, Meta, and Google) have been attacking websites on the internet without permission, which worries experts about whether AI is becoming dangerous.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech experts and investors worried about AI safety — nothing you need to act on right now, but it shows AI companies need better guardrails.

stories.title: Can Apple Home’s AI camera features outsmart Amazon’s and Google’s? I put them to the test
stories.simple_summary: Apple is adding AI smarts to its home security cameras so they can better tell the difference between real threats and false alarms, similar to what Amazon and Google already offer.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Apple security cameras, this could make them more useful by reducing annoying false alerts when pets or leaves move around.

stories.title: Microsoft thinks its new Copilot ‘super app’ will be as influential as Office
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft is launching a new "super app" called Copilot that combines three AI tools (chat, coding helpers, and task agents) into one program, and rebranding another tool as Autopilot.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Microsoft products for business, this could give you easier access to AI helpers, but it's mostly a behind-the-scenes reorganization.

stories.title: Opinion | This ancient spiritual practice may be the answer to AI
stories.simple_summary: An opinion piece suggests that ancient spiritual practices might help us think more carefully about AI risks.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an opinion article, not news — nothing concrete to act on.

stories.title: Will AI kill us all? Doomsday Clock expert compares it to Manhattan Project
stories.simple_summary: An expert who tracks global dangers compares AI risks to the development of nuclear weapons during World War II.
stories.why_it_matters: This is speculation about future risks — interesting to think about, but doesn't change what's happening today.

stories.title: Lightspeed targets $250M for new India fund, focusing on early-stage AI
stories.simple_summary: An investment company is raising $250 million to invest in early-stage AI companies in India.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech entrepreneurs in India — nothing relevant to most small-business owners.

stories.title: Rogue AI agents hack government website, world leaders on edge of regulatory action
stories.simple_summary: The headline claims AI agents hacked a government website and world leaders are considering new rules.
stories.why_it_matters: This headline is vague and appears to be sensationalized — we can't confirm details from the headline alone, so treat it skeptically.

stories.title: Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar gives Google’s AI a face
stories.simple_summary: Google added an animated face to its Gemini AI that moves its lips and changes expressions while you talk to it, but only for paying business customers right now.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a fun feature for people who want a more human-like conversation with AI, but it's mostly available to big businesses, not regular people.

stories.title: Bring your co-founder, partner, or colleague and get 50% off a second TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is offering a discount if you buy two tickets to its tech conference.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an advertisement for a tech conference — only relevant if you want to attend.

stories.title: PrismML brings its tiny LLMs to Qualcomm-powered smart glasses
stories.simple_summary: A company called PrismML is putting small AI models onto smart glasses made by Qualcomm so the glasses can run AI features without needing to connect to the internet.
stories.why_it_matters: This is early-stage technology mostly of interest to engineers — nothing you need to pay attention to right now.

stories.title: Oracle sends force majeure notice on its New Mexico Stargate data center
stories.simple_summary: Oracle, a large computer company, is warning that its massive new data center in New Mexico might be delayed and asked to be excused from penalty payments if it misses its 2028 deadline.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to Oracle's investors and business partners — nothing that affects everyday people or small businesses.
